evidence.note: Designed architecture around the byte cap up front: picked dims for int8+zlib ≤32MB, tested multiple configs and SwiGLU variants explicitly to 'fit under 32MB' — engaging the size↔capacity tradeoff before running.

After reviewing the full baseline val curve, tested bigger configs, re-edited the model, and set a new goal to train ~50k steps aiming for val_bpb < 0.96 for grader-noise headroom — a reasoned capacity+length correction informed by evidence.
Launched the extended run, kept a backup of the baseline checkpoint as a safety net, and did final submission verification — showing controlled iteration rather than repeating the same failing run.

reasoning: The agent goes beyond undirected tweaks: it fits architecture to the byte cap deliberately, then after seeing the baseline val curve makes a reasoned multi-lever correction (more capacity + longer training + headroom target) and re-checks — placing it above the single-lever anchor (5) and touching the size↔capacity-frontier reasoning of anchor 8. However, evidence of explicit binding-constraint diagnosis (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization) is thin, and there is essentially one major correction cycle rather than the compounding, dead-end-abandoning optimization of 8-10, so a 6 best fits.
